question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[-4\,\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(3-2x)] \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(3-2x)] \\  & =-4\cdot [-\frac{1}{|3-2x|\sqrt{1+(3-2x)^{2}}}]\cdot (3-2x)^{′} \\  & =\frac{4}{|3-2x|\sqrt{1+(9-12x+4{x}^{2})}}\cdot (-2) \\  & =-\frac{1}{|3-2x|}\,\frac{8}{\sqrt{10-12x+4{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
